newsitem.title: CHILE: Escondida strike drags on, no new vote seen.
newsitem.headline: Escondida strike drags on, no new vote seen.

text.p: The strike by a small group of workers at the Escondida copper mine dragged into its eighth day Friday and the union is not planning to ballot its members again on whether to continue, said a top union official.
"There is no interest in returning to work," union leader Hugo Fernandez told Reuters by telephone.
Most of Escondida's roughly 300 unionized workers, out of a total workforce of 2,000, went on strike last week after a breakdown in scheduled wage talks.
The workers voted by a majority to accept the company's wage offer in a ballot two days ago but the margin was not sufficient to end the dispute.
Under Chilean law, Escondida will be able to replace the strikers with new workers if the strike lasts over two weeks.
Fernandez repeated his claims the strike has paralyzed production at Escondida, the world's largest copper mine.
"There is no production at the mine at the moment," he said.
The pit's CEO Ken Pickering said Wednesday that output was normal and shipments unaffected by the strike. The 800,000-tonne-a-year mine is owned by Broken Hill Proprietary and RTZ Corp plc.
